system.name: PowerInfer
system.one_liner: a high-speed LLM inference engine that exploits neuron-activation locality to hybrid-serve large models on a single consumer GPU plus CPU

content.subject: how two existing offloading designs move transformer layers between CPU and GPU memory during inference

panels.label: (a) GPU-Centric Offloading
panels.differs: template: only the GPU computes; the idle CPU merely stores overflow layers, which are copied into GPU memory as needed

panels.label: (b) GPU-CPU Hybrid Offloading
panels.differs: layers are split by Transformer layer between devices; the CPU also computes on its resident layers (L1..Ln-3) and sends 'CPU Results' across PCIe for the GPU to use when computing its own layers (Ln-2..Ln)

content.key_idea: GPU-centric offloading transfers needed layers to the GPU and computes everything there; GPU-CPU hybrid offloading instead splits layers between devices, lets the CPU compute its share, then hands intermediate results to the GPU.
content.reading_order: left to right in each panel: CPU Mem contents, the CPU/GPU compute icons, then GPU Mem contents, following the numbered arrows across the PCIe bus

evidence: GPU-centric offloading utilizes CPU memory to store portions of the model parameters that exceed the GPU's capacity
Hybrid offloading distributes model parameters between GPU and CPU, splitting them at the Transformer layer level
The CPU processes its layers first, then sends intermediate results to the GPU for token generation

summary: Figure 2 contrasts two existing offloading designs for running LLMs that exceed a single GPU's memory. In (a) GPU-Centric Offloading, all computation happens on the GPU: CPU memory only stores overflow layers (L5, L6, ..., Ln), and a needed layer such as L4 is copied across PCIe into GPU memory (step 1) before the GPU processes the layers now resident there (step 2); the CPU itself stays idle. In (b) GPU-CPU Hybrid Offloading, layers are split by Transformer layer between the two devices: the CPU first computes its own resident layers (L1...Ln-3), producing 'CPU Results' (step 1), sent across PCIe to GPU memory (step 2) so the GPU can finish computing its own layers (Ln-2, Ln-1, Ln) using those results (step 3). This motivates PowerInfer's finer-grained, activation-aware split.
summary_zh: 该图对比两种offloading方案：(a) GPU中心式由GPU统一计算，所需层经PCIe传入显存，CPU仅存溢出层；(b) 混合式按层切分，CPU先算完自身层，经PCIe将结果传给GPU计算剩余层。
